docs.title: McKinsey — Who wins when AI does the shopping?
docs.description:
**Agentic Commerce Consumer Survey — ~21,000 consumers, 11 markets, June 2026.**

**The stat to quote:** AI searches hitting a *structured* product catalog convert at roughly **twice** the rate of searches relying on scraped or stale data (Shopify). That is the catalog-depth argument, made by someone else.

- **53%** of consumers now shop with AI — **India 76%**, second only to China; US trails at 48%
- **AI search is 3.2x** more influential than traditional search on the last purchase
- **Grocery and beauty** — the e-commerce laggards — are catching up fastest through agents, because agents remove friction in exactly the categories e-commerce struggled with
- Retailer assistants trail standalone AI roughly **2:1** through the journey but **draw level at checkout** (15% vs 14%) — retailers hold live inventory, payments and delivery

**Their test for a brand is ours:** *if an agent asked what a product costs, whether it's in stock, when it could be delivered and whether it could buy it now — could your systems answer?*
